guesses.decision: Read controlX/controlY(objective) without checking objective >= 0. If the activation runs with objective = -1, the host returns -1 (invalid index), so there is no runtime error. The goal is then (-1, -1), which the engine clamps.
guesses.why: The spec has no objective >= 0 guard here, unlike the default_goal/resupply/fall_back steps. The selector presumably runs this only when S.has_target_heart is on, and controlX(-1) is safe.

guesses.decision: Same as C.take_heart: no objective >= 0 guard, relying on controlX(-1) = -1 being safe.
guesses.why: Literal reading of the spec. The host returns -1 for invalid indices instead of raising an error.

guesses.decision: Used the legacy host fields carrying, ownHeartStolen, heartX and heartY exactly as written. Under rules 47 carrying and ownHeartStolen are always 0 and heartX/heartY read the enemy home, so in practice the goal is the thief (never set, see gaps) or the enemy home.
guesses.why: The spec names these fields explicitly and matches base.bas; I did not substitute control* fields.

guesses.decision: Kept the literal HP thresholds (medkit wanted below 3 HP, armor only at exactly 3 HP, medkit cost quartered at 1 HP) even though rules 49 HP runs 0-10.
guesses.why: The numbers are written into the Spec, not Params; changing them would be inventing behavior. Under rules 49 armor is rarely wanted and medkits only when nearly dead.

guesses.decision: Step 0 tests mem_tick(j) = worldTick literally, so a take is detected only when the station was in view on the immediately previous tick (mem_tick = previous tick + 1). The pickupVisible, prev_ and host state values are read once per tick and reused for Step 0c.
guesses.why: Literal reading; the runtime runs every living tick, so worldTick advances by 1 between updates.

guesses.spec_quote: whose own evidence holds and where
guesses.decision: Own evidence (and so xe_label) is evaluated only for teammate-parity bodies that reached Step 0c, that is not matched by a live friend record and not enemy parity.
guesses.why: Own evidence is defined inside Step 0c, and a body matched in Step 0a skips to the next i.

guesses.decision: Kept the literal 3 in the cost even though rules 49 HP is 0-10; the term still ranks wounded bodies first, offset by a constant.
guesses.why: The value is in the Spec, not a Param.

guesses.spec_quote: one sender never fills both witnesses
guesses.decision: When a report fills witness 1 (expired slot) and the live witness 2 has the same speaker, witness 2 is expired (xa_t2 = 0).
guesses.why: The explicit witness-1 rule does not check witness 2, so without this one sender could hold both slots and block a real second witness. Expiring the duplicate keeps the stated invariant; K.contacts also requires xa_s1 <> xa_s2.

guesses.decision: The reset is done in __recv for label L, before this message is applied, when both xa_t1(L) and xa_t2(L) are <= worldTick.
guesses.why: COM units have no per-tick SUB, and send/recv may not run on a given tick. A stale amb is harmless while both witnesses are expired, because K.contacts also requires live witnesses.

guesses.decision: A message whose cm__fa is outside 0..15 is ignored. In __send, the strong label is used only when 0 <= xe_label < 16.
guesses.why: This keeps every array index in range (AGENTS.md rule 5); the wire field width is not visible to the unit.

guesses.decision: Within means squared distance <= d_range_sq. In __recv, a cm__fa outside 0..15 is ignored.
guesses.why: Inclusive bound, plus the index guard required by rule 5.

guesses.spec_quote: Choose the one nearest to any teammate seat s with
guesses.decision: Teammate seats are s <> selfId with s MOD 2 = selfTeam. The cost of a body is its squared distance to the nearest such recently heard teammate, or to us when there is none.
guesses.why: cm__heard_* is kept per claimed sender seat, which may include enemy-parity labels; the spec says teammate.

guesses.spec_quote: Use the slot j that is within h_match of `(px, py)`
guesses.decision: Position matching for gl_* (in __recv) and hs_* (after a send) considers only slots in use (gl_until > 0, hs_t > 0), taking the lowest matching slot. Otherwise it takes the slot with the smallest gl_until or hs_t, lowest index on a tie.
guesses.why: Without this, an empty slot at (0, 0) would match a heart near the origin.

guesses.decision: release_in is sent unclamped, exactly as SK.motor reports it.
guesses.why: The spec gives no clamp; the runtime owns encoding.

gaps.need: sk_motor__sneak(1), declared in the SK.motor interface and named by every C.* quiet-approach step
gaps.substitute: Called sk_motor__sneak(1) as declared. The read-only context copy units/SK.motor.bas defines no sk_motor__sneak (nor quiet, charging, charge_x/y, charge_started or release_in), so the build depends on the assembled SK.motor matching its declared interface. The same applies to C.cover_heart, C.default_goal, C.resupply and C.fall_back.

gaps.need: sk_motor__charging, charge_started, charge_x, charge_y, release_in and quiet outputs of SK.motor
gaps.substitute: Read them as declared in the SK.motor interface; the context copy of units/SK.motor.bas does not set them yet.

gaps.need: a heart carrier / thief and carrying state
gaps.substitute: Used the legacy carrying, ownHeartStolen, heartX/heartY and K.contacts thief (from playerCarrying) as written; under rules 47+ these are constant (0 / enemy home), so thief is always -1.

lessons: A COM unit may define only its Direction SUBs (plus optional init), so cell encode/decode cannot be factored into a helper SUB; inline it in each send/recv.

Every scratch scalar a unit assigns is a whole-policy global, and 21 units with 5-30 temporaries each overflowed the 512-global limit (567). Keep temporaries and private scalar memory in one small unit-owned array (DIM <prefix>__t(N), with a comment mapping each cell), and keep named scalars for declared outputs only.
